events.text: The monsoon of the Sea of Clouds is a week late and the isle is restless. {npc} sits sewing a lantern-cover while you stand holding {gyb_piece} like a lost child. "You are pacing," {he} says. "I am deciding," you say. "You have decided," {he} says, "you are only afraid of the knot." Then {he} holds out both hands.

choices.text: Say what you are afraid of, and put it in {his} hands

effects.log: You tell it badly, which is how true things come. {npc} turns it over, finds the clasp you always catch, and fixes it with one nail. "There," {he} says.

choices.text: Ask {him} never to carry it uphill alone

effects.log: "Uphill, alone, in the dark," {he} repeats, and nods, because {he} has done all three. {He} swears, and for some reason it does not feel like a promise made to you.

choices.text: Hang it over the lantern-frame and say nothing

effects.log: It glints in the lamplight all night. In the morning {he} has tied a small red thread to the guard, the sort used on a child's wrist, and neither of you remarks on it.

events.text: The Houses hold their autumn trial of arms and you are asked to judge, which means a week in a high chair. You return to find {npc} has moved your things aside to make room, put a stand in the corner, and left a blank brocade on it. "For the starsteel," {he} says. "If you ever mean to give it up." You had not known {he} had noticed.

choices.text: Fetch {gyb_piece} and tell {him} its name, its maker, its price

effects.log: The price was a debt that took a century to clear. {npc} listens to all of it, then drapes the brocade and says that it looks better there than on you.

choices.text: Lay it on the stand, and leave it there for a year

effects.log: It stays on the stand a year. You grow used to walking past it. When you take it up again, you do it as one asks a friend's leave.

choices.text: Tell {him} it is {his} to draw, if ever you cannot

effects.log: {He} does not smile. "That will not happen," {he} says. "But I will remember you said it." The stand is moved nearer the door.

events.text: {npc} has not asked for a thing in all the years of your household, and that is how you know what {he} wants. At the foot of the White Stairs, among sellers of paper kites and plum cakes, you take {gyb_piece} from your belt and put it in {his} hands, ties and all, as if it were a bag of roasted chestnuts. {He} laughs so hard a seller turns.

choices.text: Say you could never give it to anyone else

effects.log: It is true, and so plain that {he} stops laughing. A kite-seller offers you both a plum cake without being asked.

choices.text: Say that {he} must take care of it, since you will not

effects.log: "I take care of everything," {he} says. This is truer than either of you likes. {He} wears it beneath {his} sleeve up all one hundred and eight steps.

choices.text: Buy a kite, and tie it to the hilt

effects.log: The kite goes up from the highest landing with a starsteel tail. It is the most undignified thing you have done in a century, and a small crowd cheers.

events.text: There is a rumour of raiders on the long cloud-road, and {npc} insists on travelling it for a funeral. You do not argue. You sit up all night with {gyb_piece} across your knees, trying to decide if you are a coward. At dawn you wrap it in {his} winter cloak and leave it by the door, where {he} cannot say no without stepping over it.

choices.text: Leave a note tucked in the folds

effects.log: It says four words. {npc} reads them on the road, and writes back two words, and the blade goes the whole way and returns. The note is never found again.

choices.text: Wait at the gate to hear {him} promise

effects.log: {He} comes out yawning, sees the bundle, and understands everything at once. {He} promises, and adds a condition about dinner, and goes.

choices.text: Say nothing and let {him} find it

effects.log: {He} finds it, and the cloak, and the cold tea you left for the walk. The funeral goes well. {He} sends no word of the blade, only a postcard of the weather.

events.text: A summer storm rolls over the isle just as you decide. {npc} is under the awning of the practice yard watching the rain fall through the floating stones, and you walk out with {gyb_piece} and stand beside {him}. Neither speaks. Water runs down the guard. "Is it for the rain?" {he} asks, and you realise the child in you is nearly as nervous.

choices.text: Tell {him} it is for the quiet after the rain

effects.log: It sounds like nonsense and is not. {npc} takes it as one takes a bowl of something hot, with both hands, and says that the rain is nearly done.

choices.text: Make {him} promise to oil it after every storm

effects.log: {He} promises, with the weariness of the young at the habits of the old. In twenty years {he} will say the same words to someone else.

choices.text: Pass it over, and go in to make tea

effects.log: You hear the blade drawn once, and sheathed, and the stand scraped on the flagstones. When you come out the tea is cold and {he} is smiling at nothing.

events.text: In the Cloud Library, among scrolls too old to unroll, you find {npc} reading the genealogy of a blade. Not yours: another. {He} does not look up. "It says they always break," {he} says. "Or are lost." You take down {gyb_piece} from your back and lay it on the desk, and say that yours has done neither, and you do not know how.

choices.text: Read the last page of your own entry aloud

effects.log: The page is short and the hand is hurried. {He} listens, then borrows a brush and corrects a date. "Now it is true," {he} says.

choices.text: Ask {him} to be the one who writes the next page

effects.log: {He} says that is a heavy request for a Tuesday. {He} says yes. The scribes put {his} name in the margin, very small.

choices.text: Close the scroll, and push the blade toward {him}

effects.log: The old paper sighs. {He} touches the guard and does not lift it, and you both sit in the dust of the stacks till the lamps go out.

events.text: The Eight Houses gather at the mid-autumn lantern, all their banners lined along the terrace, and you bring {npc} out before the dais with {gyb_piece} wrapped in a plain cloth. A cousin coughs. Another examines a sleeve. {npc} stands very straight, as one holds a full bowl across a crowded room. You know it is the largest silence of {his} life.

choices.text: Unwrap it slowly, so every House can see what it is

effects.log: The cloth falls. The crowd breathes. Three Houses have to decide, in front of the others, whether to bow. {npc} does not look at them. {He} looks at you.

choices.text: Have {him} say the House oath in the old tongue

effects.log: {He} says it well and stumbles on one word, and the oldest elder smiles into {his} beard. It is the smile that will hold the table for a decade.

choices.text: Hand it over in the cloth and walk away

effects.log: You leave {him} holding it in front of everyone. It is cruel, and it is correct, and you watch from the stair as {he} learns to stand.

The persimmons sit sweetly in their basket, unanswered, as the answer arrives.

choices.text: Tell {him} you want the rival to hear of it by morning

effects.log: The rival hears of it by noon. The reply is another basket, and a much smaller question. {npc} eats the persimmons and says they are sour.

choices.text: Answer the letter in {his} hand, not yours

events.text: The sky-ferry delays half a night in a thunderhead and you wait in the cabin with {npc}, who has been unusually quiet since the last Trial. The lantern swings. {gyb_piece} is in your pack. You had meant to hand it over at the isle, with ceremony, in daylight. But {he} is looking at your pack, and the cabin is small, and the thunder is long.

choices.text: Draw it, and show {him} the nicks, one at a time

effects.log: Each nick is a lesson in a form {he} already knows. By the time the storm passes {he} is asleep against the bulkhead, and you are talking to the sleeping.

choices.text: Ask {him} to keep one rule above all others

effects.log: You offer the rule. {He} asks if there is a second. There is not. The thunder goes away over the sea, and {he} repeats it, and it is a short rule.

choices.text: Let {him} hold it for the rest of the voyage

effects.log: {He} holds it for three hours, in both hands, as if it might wake. At the landing {he} hands it back correctly, and you refuse it correctly, and {he} understands.

events.text: Disciples of the isle take their own blades from the common rack, and keep them as long as they can bear. So when {npc} comes to the dawn form carrying {gyb_piece} in the wrong hand, bleary, still putting on a sleeve, a few of the younger ones nudge each other. You have given no sign. {He} has simply woken up and found it on the pillow.

choices.text: Send the rest home, and tell {him} how it came to be on that pillow

effects.log: The others go. You tell it standing in the empty yard: the late night, the thought, the choice you made without telling anyone. {He} listens with the sleeve half on.

choices.text: Run the form as always, and say nothing of it

effects.log: The form is just a form. By its end {he} has found the right hand, and the rest of the yard has found something else to look at.

choices.text: Ask {him} to name what {he} will do with it first

effects.log: "Nothing," {he} says, at last. You nod. It is the best answer you have had in a hundred years.

events.text: A letter from the Ministries names {npc} for a posting at the far edge of the Isles: three years at a cloud-fort, small pay, large honour. {He} carries it into your study as if it were the hot end of a poker. You say the post is a good one. You do not say it is dangerous. {gyb_piece} is already on the desk, and has been for an hour.

choices.text: Tell {him} what happened at the last cloud-fort you knew

effects.log: It is not a story with a good end. {He} listens through it, takes up the blade, and asks the name of the one who did not come home.

choices.text: Make {him} swear to write home, plainly, once a month

effects.log: {He} swears, and in the end writes only half of the letters, but they are the right half. You answer every one.

choices.text: Say the post is an honour, and send {him} off with the blade

effects.log: It is the truth, and you add nothing else. At the ferry {he} turns back once, and you are still on the dock, which was not part of the plan.

events.text: A cloud-merchant at the market tells you, entirely without malice, that your consort has become something of a legend in the lantern district. {npc} apparently argued down a bandit chief over the price of a mule, with {gyb_piece} at {his} hip, politely, for most of an hour. The chief left owing a bale of silk. You go home laughing, and find {him} making dumplings with flour on the guard.

choices.text: Say you heard about the mule

effects.log: {He} stops. "The mule was a fair price," {he} says, and flicks flour at you. The next market day half the stalls are quoting {him} as a savant.

choices.text: Ask how it felt to hold it in earnest

effects.log: {He} thinks it over, hands in dough. "Lighter than I thought," {he} says. "And I understood you a little." You are sorry to say that this is the whole point.

events.text: When the Houses' envoys call in unison, as they will, {npc} greets them in the gate court wearing {gyb_piece} openly over the festival silk. The envoys are courteous. It becomes noticeable only afterward that they have conceded every point: the quota, the tithe of herbs, the right of way. {npc} thanks them sweetly and sends them off with parcels of cakes.

choices.text: Tell {him} you could not have done it better

effects.log: You could have done it with more shouting. {He} accepts the praise with a bow so exact you are suspicious. By evening {he} has bought new silk.

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you the trick of the cakes

effects.log: The recipe is longer than you expected, and half of it is about waiting. In a year your own envoys are much easier to deal with.

events.text: A sparring-bout at the foot of the stairs draws a small crowd, and you arrive too late to see how it began. {npc} stands over a larger cultivator with {gyb_piece} still sheathed, shaking out a wrist. The loser stares up in plain admiration. "It was the old master's blade," the loser says to the crowd, "so of course." {npc} blinks, and does not correct them.

choices.text: Help the loser up, and say nothing yet

effects.log: The loser limps off proud. {npc} stands very still until the crowd thins, and then asks what you thought. You say the wrist is all wrong. {He} laughs with relief.

choices.text: Tell {him} the credit is truly {his}

effects.log: {He} refuses it twice. The third time {he} accepts, and the line goes round the stairs for a month.

choices.text: Take {him} to the tea-stall and say little

effects.log: Over plum tea you speak of other things. At the second pot {he} says it was very strange to be thought a copy, and then a very good one.

events.text: The heir's first season of rule brings a ledger crisis and a drought of rain-jade, and {npc} handles it by carrying {gyb_piece} to every meeting and setting it on the table, scabbard toward the door. Nobody mentions it. All the Houses speak low. The bookkeepers find, on inspection, that the ledger was only a clerk's slip. The jade comes in the next week.

choices.text: Tell {him} the sword does not solve ledgers

effects.log: "No," {he} says. "But it makes everyone read them twice." You cannot argue, and decide it is not a bad policy.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} would do if it were gone

effects.log: {He} frowns. Then {he} takes it off the table, hangs it on the wall, and holds the next meeting with only the tea. The Houses are only a little less frightened.

choices.text: Praise {him} before the council

effects.log: The council exchanges looks. By the new year there are two factions: one that likes you, and one that likes {him} more. You count this a success.

events.text: News from the southern isles: a plague of paper-wasps has closed three trade routes, and a lone swordsman with an old pattern blade cleared the worst of the swarm in a single afternoon. The southerners describe the swordsman only by the shape of the guard. {npc} has not written in a year. The shape of the guard is unmistakable. You read the account three times.

choices.text: Send a basket of wasp-salve, unsigned

effects.log: It arrives, or something like it does. The reply is a very small bag of tea with a painted wasp on the label. You keep the label.

choices.text: Tell the others at morning form

effects.log: You read the account aloud and make them do the pattern of the guard. It takes the whole morning and nobody complains.

choices.text: Make the journey south yourself

effects.log: It takes eight days. When you arrive {he} has already moved on, but the village has built a small shrine to a guard. You stand before it a while, feeling foolish and proud.

events.text: A merchant from the eastern isles sets up at your gate with a case of rare inks, and says someone named {npc} sent them. {npc} writes seldom and sends nothing but business. Inside the case, folded under the ink, is a sheet bearing only a sketch of {gyb_piece}, drawn from memory, with each nick in its place. Below is one line: "Is it still like this?"

choices.text: Draw the nicks as they are now, and send it back

effects.log: Four new nicks, a repair to the guard, and a note that the grip is darker. The sketch returns a month later with all of it added, and one more nick, which is {his}.

choices.text: Write back that nothing is as it was

effects.log: It is not the answer {he} wanted. It is the one that is true. {He} writes again that evening, three pages, and begins "I thought so."

choices.text: Keep the inks and send nothing

effects.log: You use the inks for a year. At the end you realise they were the reply, and the sketch was only the question.

events.text: A courier of the Jade Court arrives with a ledger and a small velvet bag. The ledger is a list of items seized from a fallen House. {gyb_piece} is item forty-one. The courier is clearly sorry. "They say you may claim it for the cost of its storage," says the courier, "which is four low-grade stones, and a signature."

choices.text: Pay, sign, and carry it home that night

effects.log: You pay in four low-grade stones, and sign in an unsteady hand. The velvet bag is lighter than you expected, and your arm feels the weight as an old ache.

choices.text: Pay, sign, and mount it on the wall of the hall

effects.log: It hangs there, neither used nor forgotten. Guests stop before it and are not told what it is. The fewer know, the more it is said.

choices.text: Pay the stones, and ask to have it sunk in the Sea of Clouds

effects.log: The courier writes this into the ledger, and nobody has ever refused you. It falls for hours. You hear no sound.

events.text: A pilgrim of the lower isles carries it to you on foot, wrapped in a prayer-cloth, three weeks of road in the shoes. "A traveller left it in my keeping," says the pilgrim. "They did not come back for it. I do not think they will." The pilgrim will accept nothing, not even tea. You feel the weight of that refusal as you would a coat settling.

choices.text: Take it, and pour tea nobody drinks

effects.log: The tea cools. You do not mind. Later you find the prayer-cloth is stitched with the pilgrim's name, as a courtesy, in case you wished to repay.

choices.text: Hang it in the shrine, with the pilgrim's cloth

effects.log: The cloth and the blade hang together. The next pilgrim who stops before it leaves a stone in a bowl, and then there are many.

choices.text: Walk with the pilgrim to the lower stairs and bury it there

effects.log: The pilgrim says a few words, none of them in any scripture. You do not speak. When the soil is smooth the pilgrim leaves without looking back.

events.text: The Trial of Seven Clouds ends with an auction, and a crowd gathers around a rack of retired arms. The fifth lot is {gyb_piece}. Its rust has been scoured, and a clerk reads out a provenance that is wrong in three places and right in the worst one. You have a purse in your sleeve and a seat in the third row. The bidding starts low.

choices.text: Bid, and keep bidding

effects.log: You pay far too much. The clerk looks relieved. When you walk out with it the crowd parts and you hear someone say, wonderingly, that they thought it was only a story.

choices.text: Bid, win, and donate it to the Trial hall

effects.log: The hall hangs it where every competitor must pass. You do not stay to watch. Years later a child asks you what it is, and you say you were there.

choices.text: Let it go to whoever is richer

effects.log: You sit through the entire auction and do not raise a hand. It goes to a collector of curiosities. You do not mind. Not by evening.

events.text: {npc} sends word that {gyb_piece} has been taken from a drowned boat and is yours to collect. When you arrive at the dock, {he} stands in the rain with it in the crook of both arms, soaked through, ignoring the umbrella a boy is holding over {him}. "It stayed on the bottom three weeks," {he} says. "I thought you would want it to be dry."

choices.text: Tell {him} to keep it, and to dry it properly

effects.log: "I will oil it tonight," {he} says, and does. The boy with the umbrella is given a copper and a lesson in how to set a cloth.

choices.text: Take it, and hand {him} the umbrella

effects.log: {He} is so surprised that {he} holds the umbrella over the blade first. You laugh until you are wet too.

choices.text: Ask what {he} saw down there

effects.log: {He} did not go down. {He} directed the divers from the dock for three days, in the rain, and learned their names. It is a good account of a person.

events.text: A scholar of the Heavenly Library thanks you with great ceremony for the new edition of the Ninth Liturgy. You do not know what edition they mean. events.text: You are summoned to the Heavenly Court on a minor matter and it is no matter at all: a clerk with no business, a scroll with no content, a long wait in a long hall. events.text: Three nights before the autumn assembly you rise before the bell and find {npc} in the lamp-lit scriptorium, copying with a very fine brush. "I thought it would hurt you less if you did not see it."

effects.log: {He} hands you one. You copy the next page together in the lamplight. By dawn the copies are done. It is not forgiveness exactly, but it is nearby.

choices.text: Offer {him} a better price than the buyer's, in your name

events.text: You swapped the cups two nights ago, and tonight {npc} sits down across the offering-table with a cup of nectar poured and a face of perfect calm. "That is very rude," {he} says at last, lightly. "Of you."

choices.text: Hand {him} the bundle and point to the lower stair

events.text: You gather what you have: the copies, the buyers' receipts, a fortune-teller's testimony, the stain of ink on {his} cuff. effects.log: {He} is silent. "You cannot trust me," {he} says. "That is the best part." You write the terms. {He} reads them twice, and puts a finger on the clause you least expected.

effects.log: {He} takes up {his} mantle. "That is a clean ending," {he} says. {He} does not say goodbye. The elders, filing back in, find only a cup, still warm, on the long altar.

events.text: You bring the little vial of white powder to the evening offering and set it between the dishes. {npc} looks at it, then at you. "You found the jar," {he} says. "I thought you might." {He} picks up a ladle and stirs the soup. "It was meant to make you sleep. It was meant to keep you from the Court. effects.log: {He} sets down the ladle. "There is more," {he} says. "Not tonight." You do not press. You eat the soup. It is only soup. Neither of you tastes it.

effects.log: {He} nods. "I thought so," {he} says, and finishes the soup. At dawn {he} is gone, and the carp are circling. You do not blame them.

events.text: At the spring feast of the pantheon you put a half-formed doubt into words, before the elder gods and the guests, and the sentence falls on the table with a little crash. {npc} sets down the cup. "Is this what you think of me?" {he} asks quietly. The gods look at their sleeves. Even the temple servants have stopped. You have no proof. You have only a feeling, spoken aloud.

effects.log: {He} accepts the apology with perfect grace. It is a trap you walk into smiling. The gods approve. The sanctum is warm for a month, and then it is not.

effects.log: You excuse yourself, and walk the whole length of the long cloister, and for the first time you look at every cup, every door, every hand. By the dawn bell you have a list.

events.text: The long season turns, and you find there is nothing to find. One evening {he} laughs at a joke of yours, a true laugh, and stops, startled, and looks at {his} own hands.

effects.log: The nectar is warm and ordinary. It tastes, for the first time in ages, like nectar. {He} watches you drink with a look you do not quite name.

effects.log: {He} blinks. "That I have missed you," {he} says. "Which is a silly thing to say to a god in the same room." It is the sort of silliness that holds up a roof.

events.text: It is the first day of snow on the sacred mountain, and the two of you are old enough to take your nectar on the long terrace without a word. {npc} breaks the silence. effects.log: {He} turns the hand over. "I thought you did," {he} says. The snow falls on the temple roofs in great silent flakes, and the nectar goes cold in the cups.

effects.log: You close the screen softly. The nectar is left to cool. What you needed to hear was not what you wanted, and you cannot say which of the two is the grief.
